title: Hierarchical decode: 16x16 coarse-cell classification + per-cell continuous offset regression from a layout-preserving descriptor
hypothesis: Exp 3's remaining 810 m has two structural causes baked into the flat 64x64 (108 m/cell) classification head, both fixed by the same reparameterization. (1) Never-trained-cell suppression: the frozen split holds out 360 px (360 m) eval blocks that training windows may never touch, so every cell lying inside an eval block appears ONLY as a softmax negative across all 96 epochs -- the converged model systematically pushes probability mass AWAY from exactly the cells where every eval crop lives, forcing predictions onto the ring of trained cells around each block (a >=1-2 cell, 110-250 m structural floor) and, worse, letting mass scatter to lookalike trained cells elsewhere. (2) Label starvation: 6000 training crops over 4096 cells is ~1.8 positives per cell, far too sparse to learn a 4096-way discrimination. Reparameterizing to a 16x16 coarse grid (434 m cells) + continuous within-cell offset removes both at once: eval blocks are isolated on the split's diagonal lattice (no two adjacent), so every 434 m coarse cell is guaranteed to contain trained territory (no suppressed classes), each coarse class gets ~23 positives instead of ~1.8, and the offset regressor is a continuous function that can interpolate into the unseen eval-block interior of a cell it recognizes -- discrete classes cannot interpolate, regression can. The offset needs to know WHERE in the cell the crop sits, which a global-average-pooled texture bag cannot express, so the descriptor keeps a coarse 4x4 spatial layout instead of averaging it away; this descriptor change is load-bearing for the offset head, not a separate idea.
method: In model/model.py only: replace the flat GRID=64 head with (a) a descriptor that preserves layout -- 1x1 conv 128->32 on the 8x8 feature map, 2x2 avg-pool to 4x4x32, flatten to 512 -- (b) a 256-way coarse-cell head (16x16 grid, ~434 m cells) and (c) a per-cell offset head (512->512, i.e. (du,dv) per cell, tanh-bounded to +/-0.75 cell). Output uv = posterior-weighted sum over cells of (cell center + offset); conf = max posterior mass in any 2x2 cell neighborhood. Loss = soft-label CE over the 16x16 grid (sigma 0.5 cells) + true-cell offset MSE + composed-uv MSE. model/train.py is untouched (forward_logits/loss_fn interface preserved as a tuple).
expected_outcome: Worst-case median error (the single Berlin/asis cell) drops from 810 m into the 250-500 m range. The risk profile is asymmetric: even if the offset head collapses to cell centers, correct coarse classification alone yields a ~165 m median (median distance from center of a uniform point in a 434 m cell) plus a misclassification tail -- so any result under ~600 m confirms the direction, and under 250 m means the offset regression is genuinely interpolating into unseen eval blocks and the 100 m milestone is within one refinement. If instead the score lands NEAR 810 m with high coarse accuracy in the train log, the descriptor (not the decode) is indicted. Gates: ~495k params, ~2.0 MiB fp32 ONNX (under 4 MiB), latency well under the 250 ms proxy (exp 3 was 0.63 ms). Wall-time ~15 min on MPS, same data plan and 96-epoch budget as exp 3.
eli5: The old model had to answer 'which of 4096 tiny map squares is this photo from?' -- but the exam is deliberately held on patches of Berlin the model never studied, and with 4096 choices it had only ever seen one or two examples of each. Worse, squares inside the exam patches never appeared in study material at all, so the model literally learned to never answer them. The new model first picks one of 256 much bigger neighborhoods -- big enough that every one was at least partly studied -- and then points to a spot inside it, the way you'd say 'that's Kreuzberg, near the top-left corner of the park'. Pointing is a smooth skill that transfers into the unstudied patches, where memorizing tiny squares could not.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only, no synthetic lighting variants

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: Same small CNN, but instead of blending everything into one average summary it keeps a coarse 4×4 layout of the crop — which corner has the park, where the street cuts through

stages.name: Map-grid classifier
stages.detail: Scores the 256 squares of a 16×16 checkerboard over Berlin — squares big enough that every one was at least partly seen during training

stages.name: Coordinate + confidence readout
stages.detail: Every square also learns a pointer to the exact spot inside it; the answer blends the best squares' centers plus their pointers into one (lat, lon); confidence = how much belief lands in one small neighborhood of the map

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: Same 96-pass schedule and fresh rotations as before, but the multiple-choice loss now grades the 256 big squares, and two new terms teach the pointer: 'point to the right spot inside your square' and 'the final blended answer must land on the truth'

implementation_brief:
ALL changes are in model/model.py. model/train.py must NOT be edited -- the design deliberately preserves its interface: train.py calls loss_fn(model.forward_logits(xb), yb) and export_onnx(model.cpu(), path), both of which keep working as specified below.

=== model/model.py ===

1. Module constants: replace GRID = 64 with GRID_C = 16 (coarse cells, ~434 m on the 6939 px Berlin raster). Replace LABEL_SIGMA = 1.0 with LABEL_SIGMA = 0.5 (in COARSE cell units). Remove CONF_POOL (the new confidence uses a fixed 2x2 neighborhood). Add OFFSET_SCALE = 0.75 (tanh bound on per-cell offsets, in coarse-cell units; the slack past +/-0.5 lets neighbor cells point across their boundary during soft composition). Update the module docstring's 'Current:' paragraph to describe the hierarchical decode; keep the two contract bullets verbatim.

2. _cell_centers(): same function, but over GRID_C: k = arange(GRID_C*GRID_C), cell_u = ((k % GRID_C)+0.5)/GRID_C, cell_v = ((k // GRID_C)+0.5)/GRID_C. Row-major layout (v = rows, u = cols) must stay consistent everywhere, exactly as now.

3. TinyLocNet.__init__: keep the existing conv trunk (chans [3,16,32,64,128], stride-2 convs + BN + ReLU) EXACTLY as is -- it produces an 8x8x128 map for 128x128 input. Delete self.head. Add: self.reduce = nn.Conv2d(128, 32, 1) (1x1 conv); descriptor = flatten(avg_pool2d(relu(reduce(features)), 2)) -> 4x4x32 = 512-dim. Add self.coarse_head = nn.Linear(512, GRID_C*GRID_C) (256-way logits) and self.offset_head = nn.Linear(512, GRID_C*GRID_C*2) (per-cell (du,dv)). Keep the cell_u/cell_v registered buffers (now length 256).

4. forward_logits(x): returns a TUPLE (logits, offsets): compute f = self.features(x); d = flatten(F.avg_pool2d(F.relu(self.reduce(f)), 2), start_dim=1)  # (B,512); logits = self.coarse_head(d)  # (B,256); offsets = OFFSET_SCALE * torch.tanh(self.offset_head(d)).reshape(B, GRID_C*GRID_C, 2)  # (B,256,2) in coarse-cell units. (loss_fn consumes this tuple; train.py's call site is unchanged.)

5. forward(x) (the exported inference graph): (logits, offsets) = self.forward_logits(x); p = softmax(logits, dim=1); per-cell pointed position in normalized map coords: pos_u = cell_u[None,:] + offsets[:,:,0]/GRID_C, pos_v = cell_v[None,:] + offsets[:,:,1]/GRID_C; u = (p*pos_u).sum(1, keepdim=True), v = (p*pos_v).sum(1, keepdim=True). Confidence: pm = p.reshape(-1,1,GRID_C,GRID_C); neigh = F.avg_pool2d(pm, 2, stride=1) * 4  (2x2 windows, NO padding); conf = neigh.amax(dim=(1,2,3)).unsqueeze(1).clamp(0,1). Return torch.cat([u,v,conf], dim=1) -- shape (B,3), same [[u,v,conf]] contract as now. Everything must stay ONNX-exportable with the existing export_onnx (opset 17, dynamo=False): softmax, tanh, avg_pool2d, amax, reshape, cat are all fine; do NOT use argmax/gather.

6. loss_fn(out, target_uv): signature loss_fn(out, target_uv) where out is the (logits, offsets) tuple. Three terms:
   (a) Soft-label CE, same construction as now but on the 16x16 grid: gu = target_uv[:,0]*GRID_C - 0.5, gv = target_uv[:,1]*GRID_C - 0.5; d2 over a GRID_C axis grid exactly mirroring the current row-major code; q = softmax(-d2.flatten(1)/(2*LABEL_SIGMA**2)); ce = -(q * log_softmax(logits,1)).sum(1).mean().
   (b) True-cell offset MSE: ku = clamp(floor(target_uv[:,0]*GRID_C), 0, GRID_C-1) (long), kv likewise from target_uv[:,1]; k = kv*GRID_C + ku (row-major, matching _cell_centers); true offsets du* = target_uv[:,0]*GRID_C - (ku.float()+0.5), dv* likewise (each in [-0.5,0.5]); off_sel = offsets[arange(B), k]  # (B,2); l_off = ((off_sel - stack([du*,dv*],1))**2).sum(1).mean().
   (c) Composed-uv MSE: recompute u,v exactly as forward() does (p-weighted sum of pointed positions -- factor this into a small helper used by both forward and loss_fn to avoid drift); l_uv = ((uv_hat - target_uv)**2).sum(1).mean().
   Return ce + 5.0*l_off + 10.0*l_uv. Keep/adapt the _CELL_CACHE device-cache pattern for cell centers.

7. UNCHANGED: build_model(), export_onnx() (same dummy input 1x3x128x128, output name 'uvc', opset 17, dynamo=False), estimate_position() (reads [[u,v,conf]] and converts via px_to_lonlat). Do not touch EPOCH_MULT or anything in train.py; do not touch any file in /FROZEN.

=== Fixed contracts (restated) ===
- train.py CLI: python -m model.train --area <a> --out-dir <d> [--data-dir D] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket M] [--seed S]; exports one ONNX per area at <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx.
- ONNX contract: input 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1]; output [[u, v, conf]] with u,v normalized map coords in ~[0,1] and conf in [0,1].
- Frozen gates (pipeline/score.py): ONNX file <= 4 MiB, single-thread host latency proxy <= 250 ms, coverage (conf >= 0.3) >= 0.2 or the cell scores FAIL. Expected footprint here: ~495k params, ~2.0 MiB fp32, sub-millisecond host latency.

=== Sanity checks before finishing ===
- python -c smoke: build_model(); x=torch.rand(2,3,128,128); out=model(x); assert out.shape==(2,3) and 0<=conf<=1; loss_fn(model.forward_logits(x), torch.rand(2,2)).backward() runs.
- Export ONNX to a temp path and run it once through onnxruntime with a random frame; confirm output shape (1,3) and file size < 4 MiB.
